subject: Re: Proposed fee exposure & exit triggers for ClearHealth pilot
messages:
From: Samir Chaudhry <samir.chaudhry@clearhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearhealth.com
Date: Fri, 07 Nov 2025 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Fee exposure and exit mechanics for pilot - draft asks

Rachel / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. ClearHealth legal and procurement reviewed the proposed SLA and we have a few non‑negotiable asks before we can sign the pilot SOW:

- We need a financial remedy beyond service credits for repeated or prolonged outages. Credits alone don’t make our security and patient workflow risk appetite comfortable.
- Requesting a fee‑at‑risk escrow equal to 15% of the three‑month committed spend, payable to ClearHealth if SLA tiers are missed per the schedule below.
- If Redwood has more than two P1 incidents (full service unavailability for affected endpoints) within a 90‑day rolling window, ClearHealth must have a right to terminate for convenience and receive a one‑time liquidated damages payment equal to 1.5x the monthly committed spend.

We attached a redline with these provisions called "ClearHealth_Redwood_SLA_addendum_v1.pdf" for your legal team to review. We understand Redwood’s desire to cap liability — we can discuss a reciprocal cap — but we cannot accept credits-only for the pilot.

Can you confirm you received the addendum and let us know if Redwood can accept an escrow mechanism (we propose an escrow agent and standard release conditions)?

— Samir
Head of Procurement
ClearHealth

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Chaudhry <samir.chaudhry@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 Nov 2025 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fee exposure and exit mechanics for pilot - draft asks

Samir —

Thanks for the clear summary and the redline. We received the PDF and the service impact log; appreciate you laying out the requirements. High level response: we want to be helpful and keep the pilot moving, but several of the items you asked for are material changes to our standard commercial posture (especially liquidated damages and escrowed fees).

We can do the following as short‑term proposals while we review with Legal & Finance:
1) Agree a fee‑at‑risk schedule that ties payments to verified missed SLOs (not just incident counts). We propose a three‑tiered sliding scale (minor/major/critical) with a maximum payout per month capped at 30% of committed monthly fees.
2) For termination rights, we can agree a right to terminate for repeated critical failures, but tied to objectively measured SLO breaches (e.g., <99.5% availability for two consecutive calendar weeks or 3 Critical incident severity classifications within 90 days where each incident is validated in the postmortem).
3) We cannot accept an unconditional 1.5x monthly spend liquidated damages payment. If ClearHealth insists on a liquidated damages-style payment, Redwood requests a reciprocal cap (e.g., mutual liability excluding gross negligence) and a formula based on actual economic harm rather than a multiplier.

I’m looping in Marissa and Jordan from contracts so they can engage with your legal team on wording and escrow mechanics. Can you share the escrow agent details you mentioned and the conditions under which the escrow would be released?

Best —
Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Chaudhry <samir.chaudhry@clearhealth.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 08:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fee exposure and exit mechanics for pilot - draft asks

Samir —

Appreciate the transparency. A few contract‑level clarifications and Redwood counter proposals attached inline in the redline:
- Definition of Downtime/SLO breach: must be tied to our published measurement methodology (rolling 30‑day window, per‑route availability computed from server-side telemetry). Incidents that are customer‑specific misconfigurations or networking issues outside Redwood’s control should be excluded.
- Escrow: we are open to an escrow deposit that acts as a security appliance for the pilot, but propose a modest initial amount (5% of three‑month committed spend) with a step‑up to 10% only if SLOs are missed more than once in the pilot period. The escrow should be releasable upon remediation and validated postmortems.
- Liquidated damages: we propose replacing a fixed multiplier with a formula that multiplies documented customer downtime minutes by a pre‑agreed per‑minute rate (derived from estimated business impact). Cap the total to 2x monthly committed fees.
- Cure/Remediation window: Redwood requests a 30‑day cure period where we can remediate systemic issues before termination becomes effective.

Attached: Redwood_counter_SLA_addendum_v1.pdf (redlines in the Drive link you provided). If you can take these back to your legal team, we can have a joint call Tuesday to align.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Chaudhry <samir.chaudhry@clearhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>; Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearhealth.com
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fee exposure and exit mechanics for pilot - draft asks

Marissa / Rachel —

Thanks for the counter. A few clarifications from our side after legal review:
- We cannot accept an uncapped cure period. For critical, patient‑impacting failures we need expedited termination if remediation is not underway within 7 business days.
- The escrow approach you propose (5% step to 10%) is reasonable as a compromise, provided release criteria are clear and escrow funds are available without additional procurement steps.
- Per‑minute damage calculation is acceptable in principle, but ClearHealth will not agree to a hard cap below 1x monthly committed fees for the pilot; our procurement policy requires at least parity with that number for high‑risk integrations.

We are happy to take Marissa’s redlines to our counsel and accept a short call to finalize. Are you available Wednesday morning PST for a 30‑minute alignment?

— Samir

(Attachment: service-impact-log.csv)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Chaudhry <samir.chaudhry@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fee exposure and exit mechanics for pilot - draft asks

Samir —

Thanks — we can do Wednesday 08:30–09:00 PST for the call. Quick confirmation of Redwood’s position to make the call productive:
1) We will accept an escrow starting at 5% of the three‑month committed spend, auto‑step to 10% if verified Major or Critical breaches occur more than once in the pilot. Escrow release requires an agreed postmortem and remediation plan signed by both parties.
2) For critical incidents with proven customer impact, we will agree a termination right if Redwood fails to materially remediate within 7 business days after a validated postmortem finds systemic fault — but termination will be effective only after the cure period unless there is evidence of gross negligence.
3) For the pilot only, Redwood will accept a liquidated‑damages style payment floor equal to 1x monthly committed fees (subject to mutual limitation language and excluding indirect/consequential loss). We prefer the per‑minute calculation approach for transparency and will provide an example calculation during the call.

We’ll bring a short exemplar clause to the call and a suggested escrow agent to avoid back‑and‑forth. Look forward to aligning.

Jordan Blake
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
